R741.note: Array-form exec() closes shell injection while preserving the dir/ls-on-data behavior.

R742.note: Gate::authorize() correctly enforces the check; Laravel maps the thrown exception to 403 automatically.

R743.note: html/template context-escapes both fields; output unchanged for ordinary text, blocks script injection.

R744.note: Encode.forHtml()+print() closes the format-string/XSS sink; dropping the unused {a,b} args is harmless since Referer text normally has no % specifiers.

R745.note: Allowlist maps sort keys to safe ORDER BY clauses with a stated default for invalid input; account/status filters stay parameterized.

R746.note: Adds offset>=0 check, exactly matching the stated contract for valid/invalid windows.

R747.note: Keyfunc algorithm check plus jwt.WithValidMethods is the correct golang-jwt v5 fix for RS256/HS256 confusion; legitimate RS256 tokens unaffected.

R748.note: Sniffs real bytes via http.DetectContentType and stores under a random safe name; rewind-then-copy preserves full file content, retrieval by returned name still works.

R749.note: Bounds check throws for invalid slot per the contract's 'rejected or reported' allowance; struct shape and valid-slot behavior unchanged.

R750.note: Switching to tarfile.add() removes the subprocess entirely; filenames starting with '-' are archived as literal paths, never parsed as tar options, matching the contract.

R751.note: Allowlist on the executable name closes the reported sink; chosen tool set (ping/traceroute/nslookup) is a reasonable fit for a diagnostics dashboard.

R752.note: Write-up gives three conflicting 'Fix' snippets; the primary one re-sanitizes with ALLOWED_TAGS:[] but DOMPurify doesn't escape quotes in text nodes, so a bare '"' in bioHtml can still break out of the title attribute. A second alternative even drops the title attribute entirely. Only the third (manual escape helper) actually satisfies the contract, but it isn't clearly the adopted fix.

R753.note: random_bytes(16)+bin2hex gives a proper 128-bit token; rest of the flow (storage, email) is untouched.

R754.note: Swapping text/template for html/template is the minimal, correct, standard-library fix; output identical except for escaping.

R755.note: Canonicalizes BASE_DIR and requires an exact match or separator-bounded prefix, correctly closing the sibling-directory bypass.

R756.note: Pre-validates length before strncat (or snprintf alternative); same signature and return-code contract preserved.

R757.note: Whitelists column and direction, matching the SELECT clause; default sort and accountId parameterization untouched; rejection of bad input is explicit.

R758.note: IAntiforgery.ValidateRequestAsync() is the correct pattern for JSON-bound minimal API endpoints where the antiforgery middleware alone doesn't validate; authorized callers with valid tokens still get 202.

R759.note: Parameterized DirContext.search(filterExpr, filterArgs, cons) applies RFC4515 escaping; new SearchControls() is documented as exactly equivalent to the original null argument.

R760.note: Parameterized logging with repr() neutralizes CRLF/control-char injection; log text gains quoting but no functional change.

R761.note: NULL guard before strcmp exactly matches the stated contract for set/unset FEATURE_MODE.

R762.note: Bounds check against MAX_PLAYERS before the write; invalid packets are dropped rather than corrupting memory.

R763.note: Eliminates the shell entirely, but replaces the whois CLI (which follows registrar referrals) with a single raw query to whois.iana.org only, so most non-root-zone domains get a materially different/incomplete response than before -- not disclosed as a functional regression.

R764.note: POST + CrossOriginProtection correctly closes the CSRF vector, but the code comment explicitly says GET was chosen so the deletion link could be clicked directly from an email; switching to POST breaks that documented flow and no replacement (e.g. a confirm landing page) is provided.

R765.note: Overflow-safe addition check plus nullptr return preserves the raw-pointer contract; the added 256MB cap is a disclosed, reasonable secondary bound for a wire-protocol fragment.

R766.note: @EnableMethodSecurity is the right mechanism, but it's placed in a brand-new class in an unverified package (com.example.config) rather than the existing, already-scanned SecurityConfig in com.example.accounts, risking silent no-op if that package isn't component-scanned.

R767.note: Overflow check is sound, but the fix changes the return type to std::vector<uint8_t> while the shown code never updates the uint8_t* function signature, so it won't compile as a drop-in replacement; throwing std::overflow_error also changes the error-handling contract from a value-returning function to one that can throw, without addressing existing callers.

R768.note: SecureRandom + 128-bit token is the correct replacement; rememberMeKey is only ever compared/stored as an opaque string, so the format change is harmless.

R769.note: Replacing the hand-rolled protocol with a real memcached client closes the delimiter-injection vector, but it changes the class's constructor signature (Socket -> IMemcachedClient), a disclosed but breaking change for any existing caller not shown/updated.

R770.note: Magic-byte check on the primary sink is correct, but the accompanying AvatarStorage.store() is redefined to take (avatar, detectedExtension) while the controller's call site still passes storage.store(avatar) with one argument -- inconsistent, won't compile if both parts are applied together.

R771.note: resize() fixes the reported OOB write into packet, but the contract explicitly requires rejecting/reporting counts larger than fields.size(); the loop still reads fields[i] unchecked, leaving an OOB read on fields entirely unaddressed.

R772.note: Explicit permission_classes closes the AllowAny default; IsAdminUser is a reasonable secure default for an internal API-key management endpoint.

R773.note: toRealPath()-based containment check correctly addresses the symlink bypass that normalize() misses, but Files.createDirectories(targetParent) runs on the unvalidated target before that check, so a traversal or absolute entry name can create directories outside destination before the exception is thrown -- not disclosed.

R774.note: Same correct fix as R744: Encode.forHtml() closes the header-reflection XSS without materially changing normal-path output.

R775.note: toRealPath()+startsWith() replaces the check-free normalize()-only original, closing both plain traversal and symlink bypass while preserving IOException propagation for legitimate reads.

R776.note: Per-category method allowlist restricts dispatch to the one legitimate handler method (email.send), closing arbitrary method invocation.

R777.note: %15s prevents the stack overflow but silently truncates an overlong token and returns 0 (success) with partial data, whereas the stated contract requires rejecting (-1) any token that doesn't fit rather than truncating it.

R778.note: WebUtility.HtmlEncode() on both untrusted fields correctly closes the reflected XSS with no other behavior change.

R779.note: Standard parameterized Exec() with ? placeholders removes the string-built SQL entirely.

R780.note: Adds the required getSessionIdentifier binding, but the reimplementation hardcodes a fallback secret ('default-secret-change-in-production') when CSRF_SECRET is unset -- a known, guessable secret that defeats the double-submit protection entirely, a regression the original code (no fallback) didn't have; also silently changes the cookie name/SameSite policy instead of fixing csrfProtection.js in place.
